text: The committee decision is served by API-S7-002 on the write-off base as POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision under /api/recovery/writeoff/v1, with CommitteeDecision in and the decision record out; the TSD names the answer element DecisionLogEntry, which is read as the record this service returns from the local decision-record library.
why: TSD S7 T-A.1 and T-A.2 publish the operation, its purpose and its error codes with the two element names, but publish no property list and no answer body, while the step must return something to SCR-27. Naming the answer after the ledger element while the service keeps the local record of DP-03 would misdescribe the boundary.

No source this story may read names the owner of delegation_limit, and inventing a value would be a business value.

text: This story claims the approve and the escalation only: R-WO-15 writes APPROVED and R-WO-12 writes ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE, and the credit approval committee's own approve and reject out of that state (R-WO-13, R-WO-14) are claimed by no story of this key and are recorded as an open exit.

text: The legacy 'decision log' of AC1 and AC4 is read as two records: the local decision record of DP-03 written through the library in the caller's transaction before the write_off row changes, and the ledger entry decision_log_entry that rwb-decision writes; this service writes the first and keeps the identifier of the second on write_off.decision_log_id.
